newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Demerged EMI to post healthy H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Demerged EMI to post healthy H1.

text.p: EMI Plc, one of the world's big five record companies, is expected to report healthy interim profits of between 90 and 120 million stg on Tuesday despite signs of a slowdown in the global music market.
The figures for the six months to September 30 will be the first time that EMI has reported as a separate company following its demerger from rentals business Thorn Plc in August.

EMI Group comprises EMI Music plus the HMV and Dillons music and book stores. Its artists and library include Frank Sinatra, The Beatles, Janet Jackson, the Smashing Pumpkins and British newcomers The Spice Girls.
Analysts said they would be as interested in what EMI had to say about the outlook for the crucial Christmas period as the results for the first six months.
"They tend to schedule a lot of their key releases for the second half and that can make for rather dull interims," said one analyst.
The initial pre-Christmas signs are good, with bumper sales of "The Beatles Anthology 3" reported and the album topping the charts in the United States.

Fears over sales have recently sent a chill through the industry. Global retail music sales have stalled this year after climbing from $14 billion in 1986 to $40 billion in 1995, according to figures from the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry.
Rival music company PolyGram last month announced it was taking a $90 million charge as a result of a restructuring at its music division in which 400 jobs will go.
EMI shares have dropped almost 20 percent from their late summer highs on worries about the direction of the record industry as a mooted bid failed to materialise.
